newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank shares down on aid for NCB.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank shares down on aid for NCB.

text.p: Shares in the banking sector were mostly weaker on Friday morning, as worries over the sector increased after the news that Japanese financial authorities are considering asking major Japanese banks to provide funds to aid debt-ridden Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), traders said.
By 0120 GMT, shares in Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd had lost 30 yen to 1,350. Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd dropped 80 yen to 1,970.
Meanwhile, NCB shares gained four yen to 295. Its volume of 6.782 million shares was ranked as the heaviest.

Japanese financial authorities are considering asking Japan's major city banks to provide about 70 billion yen to buy new NCB shares in order to help the bank restructure, banking sources said on Friday.
They also said the Bank of Japan (BOJ) is mulling channelling 80 billion yen to NCB through a special fund failed "jusen" mortgage firms.
"Selling pressure of bank shares is potentially strong, and a sharp fall could be triggered again," said a securities house trader.
